name: limit_property_on_a_configuration_that_does_not_exist
why: THE MOST IMPORTANT REFUSAL OF THE ENTRY, and the easiest one not to make. `get_CustomPropertyManager("Right")` on a configuration that does not exist raises NOTHING: it returns a manager, and `Add3` on that manager answers «AddedOrChanged». The property is written, the code is happy, and in the file it is not there. It is the defect that gives no error in its purest form: the whole chain says yes.
_why_the_name_is_checked_first: The only way to catch it is to ask the document which configurations it declares BEFORE writing. The check cannot come after -- afterwards, everything went well.
